hypothesis: Daily unlock releases and half the emissions will cut the quarterly sell waves and lift the drawdown score.
rationale: Quarterly lumps of team and investor tokens hit the pool at once, and farmers dump 60% of 2%/month emissions.

hypothesis: Stretching team vesting from 12 to 36 months will cut daily team selling enough to lift stability.
rationale: Team tokens have a $0.005 cost basis, so the team sells about 60% of every unlock.

hypothesis: A $3M protocol pool, a 5%/day buyback on 30% dips with a 12-month reserve, and a 12-month investor drip with emissions off will keep depth and drawdown in range.
rationale: The worst pool depth sits below the $3M target, the month-3 investor cliff lands as one wave, and a reserve stops buybacks eating the opex runway.

hypothesis: A $13M pool would make price impact negligible.
rationale: Depth is the strongest lever on drawdown in the dev runs.

hypothesis: Putting $6M into the pool should buy stability at little runway cost.
rationale: Depth helps drawdown and liquidity, and the raise can fund it.

hypothesis: Cutting the protocol pool to $0.5M, dropping the buyback and a 6-month investor drip frees about $4M of runway while mercenary LPs keep depth above target.
rationale: In every dev run the $4M of outside liquidity alone keeps the pool above $3M, so protocol depth only costs runway; shorter locks raise more.

hypothesis: Turning emissions back on at 1%/month should bring in enough buyers to lift the price.
Monthly instead of daily releases should mean fewer sell events.
rationale: Each release day triggers a fresh sell decision by every cohort.
